memoryArchitectureDecision.summary: Use AzA as the single canonical brain for durable records, provenance, access control, search, and projection history. Keep granular per-agent skills, prompts, tools, sessions, and working memory in Codex, Hermes, and agent runtimes. Promote durable facts back into AzA with source, agent, session, sensitivity, and evidence labels.
memoryArchitectureDecision.whyNotSingleFlatVault: A single flat vault would blur permissions, stale runtime state, raw logs, and secrets. It would also make it hard to tell which agent produced which fact.
memoryArchitectureDecision.whyNotFullySeparateBrains: Fully separate agent brains would fragment GTM, product, architecture, and customer knowledge. Cross-agent routing needs one canonical memory graph.

summary: This map consolidates the current PC architecture into one source-of-truth plan: LobeHub is the harness, Codex is the coding executor, VAN is the active runtime workspace, AzA is the canonical brain target, VANTA-Brain is a reviewed projection vault with partial live coverage evidence, workspace roots are reconciled by metadata and ownership policy, the agent fleet is metadata-mapped into granular overlays, the daily command workflow is read-only/manual until durable AzA gates pass, and app/device/browser surfaces remain approval-first until live adapters and approvals are implemented.
